### Using the prefix option

If your project has class names that conflict with Tailwind CSS utilities, you can prefix all Tailwind-generated classes and CSS variables using the `prefix` option:

<CodeExampleStack>

```css
/* [!code filename:app.css] */
/* [!code word:important] */
@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);
```

```css
/* [!code filename:Compiled CSS] */
/* [!code word:tw\:] */
@layer theme {
  :root {
    --tw-color-red-500: oklch(0.637 0.237 25.331);
  }
}

@layer utilities {
  .tw\:text-red-500 {
    color: var(--tw-color-red-500);
  }
}
```

</CodeExampleStack>

content.text:
Not quite safe by default, but Tailwind v4 does have an escape hatch: the `prefix()` option.

**docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx, "Using the prefix option"**: `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` prefixes **both** generated classes and theme CSS variables, e.g. `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500`.

So if you use `prefix(tw)`, all built-in theme variables get namespaced (`--tw-color-red-500`, etc.), avoiding collisions with your users' site variables — and you can still use utilities like `rounded-lg` since they compile to prefixed classes/vars too. This solves your exact problem without needing to strip unused variables manually.
